governance_context.executive_summary: The project builds part of the ARC genomics application and delivers QA test automation across four sequential milestones: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch. Toptal develops the micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend (React/Next.js), FastAPI services and nomenclature service on Snowflake and Azure AD/MSAL, and writes automated tests (Playwright, Jest, Pytest) for both Toptal-built and Client-built components. The Client owns platform infrastructure, the data tier, and remediation of defects in its own components.

charter.project_purpose: Build the scientist-facing ARC application within the Client's larger genomics platform and provide automated QA coverage across the full ARC program.
delivery_objectives: Build the micro-frontend shell with global navigation, routing, Azure AD/MSAL authentication and the Client's design system.
Implement FastAPI search, detail, asynchronous query, OneGWAS direct-write and haplotype services over Snowflake.
Build the ARC micro-frontend with faceted search, result detail and PHG/GATSBY interval visualization, plus the nomenclature service.
Deliver automated test scripts, execution and defect reports for Toptal-built and designated Client-built components.
Run integration, UAT and hardening cycles and complete production smoke testing with a 48-hour defect watch.
success_criteria: Each milestone is accepted through its own acceptance gate and sign-off, with UAT run after each milestone.
Search P95 latency under 1 second and detail P95 under 500ms.
Shell load P95 under 3 seconds and authentication success at 100%.
Frontend unit test coverage at or above 80%, with accessibility tests passing.
All critical and high defects in Toptal-built work closed and full regression green before cutover.
Production smoke tests pass 100% with a clean 48-hour defect watch.
high_level_scope: P1 Foundation (weeks 1-6): micro-frontend shell, Azure AD/MSAL authentication, end-to-end test harness, pipeline quality gates, security testing and data model validation.

P2a Services and Data (weeks 7-16): FastAPI search and detail endpoints, asynchronous query processing, performance spike, OneGWAS direct-write integration and validation of Client-built ingestion pipelines.
P2b Application Surface (weeks 17-21): ARC micro-frontend faceted search, result detail and haplotype visualization, haplotype endpoints, nomenclature service and related test suites.

P3 Launch (weeks 22-26): integration, performance, security and cross-browser (Chrome and Edge) testing, UAT execution, hardening iteration, production smoke tests, MTA Store parity confirmation and training documentation.
exclusions: Platform infrastructure, DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring and security design/hardening (Client-owned).
Architecture and design stories, Snowflake data model design, and data ingestion and migration builds (Client-owned).
Remediation of defects in Client-built components, and achievement of numeric targets for Client-built work.
Hypercare beyond the 48-hour defect watch, post-launch maintenance, and go-live planning and production deployment.
Creation, extension or maintenance of the Client's design system, and UAT coordination and sign-off.

assumptions: Milestones run sequentially as acceptance gates: P2a starts when HS-4781 (Snowflake schema DDL) is complete, P2b starts after P2a is accepted, and P3 starts after P2b is accepted.

UAT is included in the fixed price, limited to two runs per milestone and covering all work, not only Toptal-built work; further runs need a change order.
The Cogen API is assumed to be about 95% available and stable; failures and re-tests caused by lower availability need a change order.

The client design system is reused for all screens; estimates cover integrating it and building a limited number of ARC-specific components (count not yet defined), and further components or design system changes need a change order.
Changes outside Toptal's control that force extra test cycles or script rework (e.g., upstream Snowflake schema changes, API taxonomy shifts, design-system changes) need a change order.
Re-testing after the client fixes a failed Certification target is covered once; additional re-runs need a change order.
Client stakeholders are available for meetings, and the client is responsible for the legal and regulatory compliance of the product.

platform_environment_commitments: Client owns the platform layer (Terraform, infrastructure) and the data tier (ingestion pipelines, Snowflake data model); Toptal owns the ARC application (shell, micro-frontend, FastAPI services, nomenclature service).
Snowflake is the data platform hosting ARC tables, provided by the client; Toptal services read and write to it and tests run against it.
Azure AD/MSAL is the identity provider and authentication library, provided by the client.
Azure Key Vault (secrets for CI/CD) and CloudFront (hosted by the platform shell) are provided by the client.
Client maintains the dev, staging and production environments; integration testing runs in staging at production-like volume.
Test frameworks (Playwright, Jest, React Testing Library, Pytest) are listed as provided by the client during the engagement.
Cogen and Tagasys external APIs are provided by the client and are in test scope.
Third-party items provided or recommended by Toptal are as-is without warranty, and the client is responsible for post-delivery licenses for work done in third-party tools.

sow_interpretation.approval_expectations: Each milestone is an acceptance gate with its own sign-off. The client has 5 business days from notice of completion to review and give written notice of failure, otherwise the milestone is deemed accepted (also if used in production). The client signs a milestone acceptance certification through its designated approvers (Mike Magwire and Satya). Failed items get written non-conformance details and up to three rework attempts. Weekly status reports require written confirmation or feedback, and a Milestone Acceptance Review is held at the end of each milestone.

decisions.decision_text: The engagement is Fixed Fee with milestone billing, totaling $200,365 across four milestones, each invoiced on completion.
decisions.rationale: Syngenta accepted the fixed-price four-phase model. Milestone fees: $26,808 (P1), $60,356 (P2a), $68,210 (P2b), $44,991 (P3).

decisions.decision_text: Delivery runs in four sequential phases (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch). Each phase is an acceptance gate with its own deliverables, acceptance criteria and sign-off, and UAT runs after each.
decisions.rationale: The phases follow Syngenta's own plan, with P2 split on a real technical dependency boundary. Sign-off comes from Mike Magwire and Satya.

decisions.decision_text: Syngenta owns the platform layer (Terraform, infrastructure) and the data tier (ingestion pipelines, Snowflake data model). Toptal owns ARC application development: the micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI services and nomenclature service.
decisions.rationale: This ownership split was stated by Syngenta's technical lead and defines who builds, and who remediates defects in, each component.

decisions.decision_text: Toptal delivers automated QA test scripts, their execution and defect reports for both Toptal-built and Syngenta-built components, rather than manual QA. Testing is against the full platform, with SSO and external integrations in test scope.
decisions.rationale: This is the position Syngenta stated. Automated scripts make test coverage durable rather than a one-off pass.

decisions.decision_text: Toptal tests and certifies Syngenta-built components, but Syngenta remediates failures. Numeric targets on Syngenta-built work (e.g., PubMed precision, GWAS Atlas coverage, taxonomy coverage, referential integrity) are Syngenta's to achieve and are not a condition of accepting Toptal's work.
decisions.rationale: Writing a test for a component is not a guarantee that the component meets its target. Toptal re-runs scripts after remediation, and additional re-runs go through Change Order.

decisions.rationale: Toptal-built components run on Syngenta-owned Snowflake, Azure AD, CloudFront and upstream systems that Toptal does not control.

commercial_guardrails.contract_type_implication: Fixed Fee with milestone billing (total $200,365), so Toptal absorbs any effort overrun on in-scope work. Any change to scope, timing, client responsibilities or assumptions must go through a Change Order.
commercial_guardrails.billing_consumption_assumption: Fees are invoiced on completion of each milestone, not by timesheet hours: M1 P1 Foundation $26,808 (Nov 17, 2026), M2 P2a Services and Data $60,356 (Jan 26, 2027), M3 P2b Application Surface $68,210 (Mar 2, 2027), M4 P3 Launch $44,991 (Apr 6, 2027). The client has 5 business days to accept each milestone, and is notified in writing (email is enough) if the actual completion date differs from the estimate.
commercial_guardrails.staffing_assumption: Team size, roles and hours are not specified. Delivery Manager is Saadia Iqbal, and the team joins the client's daily standups. The schedule assumes no holiday stoppages and no client buyout of Toptal talent, and no design/UX role is yet assigned on either side.
commercial_guardrails.commercial_exposure_note: Margin is exposed to client-side dependencies: Toptal work cannot start until the related client-built work is done (notably the Snowflake schema before P2a), and the lowest-confidence pipelines are client-built. Toptal also tests the full platform, UAT is capped at two runs per milestone, and three failed remediation attempts on a milestone let the client terminate (work in progress is still payable).
commercial_guardrails.approved_work_rule: Only the work and test automation listed under the four milestones (P1, P2a, P2b, P3), plus Change Orders approved in writing, may be executed. This includes up to two UAT runs per milestone, one re-execution of tests after client remediation, and the 48-hour post-deployment defect watch.
commercial_guardrails.non_approved_work_rule: The following need a written Change Order before any work starts: platform/DevOps, security design, architecture and design stories, Snowflake data model work, ingestion/migration builds, and creation or maintenance of the client design system. The same applies to remediation of client-built defects, extra UAT runs or test re-runs, testing of other client components, rework from upstream schema or taxonomy changes, Cogen availability below ~95%, and hypercare or post-launch maintenance beyond the 48-hour watch.
commercial_guardrails.work_at_risk_rule: Work-at-risk requires written PMO Lead approval and executive exception sign-off. This covers any work before the October 7, 2026 effective date or beyond the approved milestone scope and fees.
commercial_guardrails.change_control_trigger: A Change Order is triggered by changes to scope, timeline or cost, or by a failed assumption. Examples are upstream Snowflake schema changes, API taxonomy shifts, design-system changes, UAT runs beyond two per milestone, extra test re-runs, and Cogen availability below ~95%. A mutually agreed start-date shift alone does not need one, because completion dates shift to match.
commercial_guardrails.change_order_route: PMO Lead leads -> Delivery Manager (Saadia Iqbal) aligns client contact (Mike Magwire) -> Client approves -> Contracting issues the Change Order.
